models.name: todo_list_users
models.description:
Regular user accounts for the Todo list application.

Represents authenticated users who can create and manage their personal todo items. Each user account is identified by a unique email address and secured with a hashed password. Users register through the public registration flow and gain immediate access to create their personal todo lists.

User accounts are completely isolated from each other - users can only view and manage their own todo items. The system enforces strict data boundaries to ensure privacy and security across all user operations.

This table stores core authentication credentials and account metadata. Session management for users is handled through the related todo_list_user_sessions table, which tracks JWT refresh tokens and connection information for security and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's email address used for authentication and unique identification. Must be unique across all user accounts. Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for consistency and case-insensitive comparison.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed user password using industry-standard hashing algorithms (bcrypt or argon2). The original password is never stored in plain text. This hash is used to verify user credentials during authentication.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created. Automatically set during registration and never modified thereafter. Used for account lifecycle tracking and analytics.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the user account. Updated whenever account information changes, such as password updates or email modifications.

models.name: todo_list_user_sessions
models.description:
User authentication sessions for JWT refresh token management.

Tracks active user sessions to support JWT-based authentication with access and refresh tokens. Each session represents a user's authenticated connection from a specific device or browser. Sessions store connection context (IP address, URL, referrer) for security auditing and troubleshooting.

Sessions are created when users log in and expire based on the refresh token lifetime (typically 7-30 days). The expired_at field tracks when a session ends, either through explicit logout, token expiration, or security-related revocation (such as password changes).

This table enables session revocation capabilities essential for security operations like logout, password resets, and "logout from all devices" functionality. Multiple concurrent sessions per user are supported to allow access from different devices simultaneously.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who owns this session. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was established. Used for security monitoring, audit trails, and identifying suspicious authentication patterns.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL where the authentication request originated. Provides context about the application entry point for this session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating the page or source that led to the authentication request. Helps track user navigation patterns and authentication flow origins.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created through user login. Marks the beginning of this authenticated session period.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session ended or will end. Null for active sessions. Set when user logs out, token expires, or session is revoked for security reasons (password change, admin action).

models.name: todo_list_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts with elevated system privileges.

Represents system administrators who have elevated permissions for user management, system monitoring, and administrative operations. Admins authenticate using the same JWT-based mechanism as regular users but receive tokens with admin role and expanded permissions.

Admins can perform operations beyond regular user capabilities including viewing all user accounts, managing user status (activation/deactivation), accessing system-wide statistics, and supporting users by viewing their data for troubleshooting purposes. All administrative actions are logged for accountability and security auditing.

Admins also have their own personal todo lists separate from their administrative functions. When managing todos, admins operate under the same constraints as regular users - they can only manage their own personal todo items.

Admin accounts are created through separate administrative processes rather than public registration. The authentication and session management follows the same secure patterns as regular users to maintain consistent security posture across all actor types.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Administrator's email address used for authentication and identification. Must be unique across all admin accounts. Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for consistency.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed administrator password using industry-standard hashing algorithms (bcrypt or argon2). Admins must use strong passwords meeting the same security requirements as regular users.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created. Used for account lifecycle tracking and administrative auditing purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the administrator account. Updated when account credentials or information changes.

models.name: todo_list_admin_sessions
models.description:
Administrator authentication sessions for JWT refresh token management.

Tracks active administrator sessions with the same JWT-based authentication pattern used for regular users. Admin sessions store refresh token information and connection context to enable secure session management and revocation capabilities.

Administrative sessions follow identical lifecycle patterns to user sessions but grant elevated permissions through the admin role encoded in JWT tokens. Session tracking enables security features like logout, password reset requiring re-authentication, and "logout from all devices" functionality.

Connection context (IP, URL, referrer) is recorded for each admin session to support security auditing and investigation of administrative actions. This provides accountability and helps detect unauthorized access attempts to administrative functions.

Multiple concurrent admin sessions are supported to allow administrators to access the system from different devices or browsers simultaneously without interfering with each other.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who owns this session. {@link todo_list_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the admin session was established. Critical for security monitoring and detecting unauthorized administrative access attempts.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL where the admin authentication request originated. Provides context about the admin interface entry point for this session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating the source that led to the admin authentication request. Helps track administrative access patterns and entry points.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin session was created through administrator login. Marks the beginning of this authenticated administrative session.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin session ended or will end. Null for active sessions. Set when admin logs out, token expires, or session is revoked due to password change or security actions.

models.name: todo_list_todos
models.description:
User todo items representing tasks to be completed.

Stores individual task entries created by authenticated users for personal task management and productivity tracking. Each todo item belongs to exactly one user and maintains complete data isolation between users.

Todos capture essential task information including the task title, completion status, and temporal metadata for creation, updates, and completion tracking. The completion status allows users to track progress on their tasks, while timestamps provide historical context.

Soft deletion is supported through the deleted_at field to maintain audit trails while allowing content removal. Users can create unlimited todos, mark them complete or incomplete, and delete them as needed.

The todo list is the core feature users interact with daily to manage their personal productivity and track task completion.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who owns this todo item. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Todo item title describing the task to be completed. Required field containing the main task description that users see in their todo list. Supports up to 500 characters to allow detailed task descriptions.

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Completion status indicating whether the task has been finished. False indicates the todo is pending and needs to be done. True indicates the task has been marked as complete by the user. Users can toggle this status to mark tasks complete or revert them to incomplete.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo item was created. Automatically set when the user creates a new todo. Used for chronological ordering and displaying when tasks were added. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this todo item. Updated automatically whenever the todo is modified, including completion status changes. Tracks the most recent change for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was marked as completed. Null when the todo is not completed or has been reverted to incomplete status. Set automatically when user marks the todo as complete. Provides historical context about when tasks were finished.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for audit trail support. Null for active todos. Set when user deletes the todo to support potential recovery and maintain historical records. Enables soft delete functionality while preserving data integrity.
